issuing_body: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs
title: Fraud Tourists Plead Guilty to Minneapolis Medicaid Fraud
notes: Retrieved successfully via a plain WebFetch on the first attempt (opa/pr path, unlike usao-mn/pr paths which were Akamai-challenged for this corpus). Cited on the live /status/ page (Housing Stabilization Services section) without this corpus previously having captured it; this record closes that provenance gap. Concerns Housing Stabilization Services (HSS), not Feeding Our Future.
supports: Anthony Waddell Jefferson, 37, and Lester Brown, 53, both of Philadelphia, pleaded guilty on February 9, 2026 to one count of wire fraud each, in connection with a scheme targeting Minnesota's Housing Stabilization Services Medicaid program.
Each faces a maximum statutory penalty of 20 years in prison.
The two defendants marketed themselves as 'The Housing Guys,' traveled to Minnesota to recruit homeless shelter residents as purported clients, and billed for services never provided.

The release states the defendants used ChatGPT to generate fake client notes when documentation was requested, which the release characterizes as marking the first AI-assisted healthcare-fraud charges in Minnesota.
The scheme is alleged to have stolen approximately $3.5 million from the Housing Stabilization Services program between February 2022 and June 2025, affecting roughly 230 Medicaid beneficiaries.
Attorney General Pamela Bondi is quoted in the release: 'Criminal fraud not only robs taxpayers — it shatters trust in our institutions.'
does_not_support: A sentencing outcome for either defendant; the release covers only the guilty pleas.
Any connection between this HSS-program scheme and the separate Feeding Our Future child-nutrition prosecutions; these are different programs and different defendants.
